content.comment_body: I have a hygrosensor con-hy-ana-10v that outputs 0V for 0% humidity and 10V for 100%. The sensor uses +12V, 0V, and a signal line. There are two extra connectors for temperature and shielding, but these are not wired on the sensor. I connected +12V to one of the L+ terminals on the [product_name] module, 0V to the M connector, and the signal to input I1. In the system, I set up an analog threshold switch (we use the same type for temperature measurement and switching). I set the minimum to 0 and maximum to 100, so the system automatically calculated a gain of 0.10. On a display, where I also have two measurements from an expansion module, I selected B004-AX but it shows zero.

In [product_name] configuration software, assign the first analog input on the extension unit to Ai3 and the second to Ai4. The device offers different ways to configure the analog inputs. Check the manual for details.
Yes, I realized that on the device itself, I1 and I2 correspond to A13 and A14. I was using the wrong connection. Thank you for pointing this out.

An analog threshold switch (not sure about the English term) can be set up in the configuration menu. You can change the menu language to German under Extras - Options - Language. If the option isn't available, you can download it using the update function (Help - Update Center - continue - Internet - continue).

analysis.insight_summary: The user had trouble reading correct values from an analog hygrosensor due to incorrect wiring of the input channels on the [product_name] system. Other participants clarified the labeling and configuration for analog inputs both on the hardware and in the software. The user identified the wiring mistake and confirmed that correcting it resolved the issue.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated an easy hardware connection and immediate accurate analog readings, using typical programming methods for temperature sensing and switching.
